To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the incidence of liver cirrhoses is increasing in Egypt and the most common causes are hepatitis B and hepatitis C.
aflatoxin exposure and HBV and HCV infections were associated with liver cirrhoses, while the development of HCC was associated with aflatoxin exposure in addition to HBV infection.
the levels of mutant P 53, sIL2R and aflotoxin B1 were significantly increased in cirrhotics as well as HCC patients compared to controls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of aflatoxin and P53 mutation in hepatocarcinogenesis.
the inter-relationship among HBV and HCV infections, aflatoxin B(1) and the P53 and s IL-2R in the pathogenesis of liver cirrhoses and HCC.
the interrelationship among aflatoxins, HBV and HCV infections, mutant P53, and sIL- 2R, and the possible role of these factors in the development of HCC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
aflatoxin exposure and HBV infection act synergistically to induce the 249ser mutation in HCC.
aflatoxin B, mutant P53 & s-IL-2R may be considered as useful markers for the diagnosis of HCC in patients with cirrhotic liver.
aflatoxin B 1, P53 gene and serum IL-2 receptor may be considered as important factors in the development of HCC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

aflatoxins, HBV, HCV and P53 gene mutations may be involved in the development of liver cirrhoses and HCC. sIL-2 receptors may reflect the stimulation and proliferation of lymphocytes, monocytes or macrophages.

the 249ser mutant P53 gene is an indicator for the development of HCC in cirrhotics, and the sIL-2 R level is a good indicator for the progression of cirrhosis to HCC, while aflatoxin B 1 may be a risk factor for both cirrhosis and HCC.
the 249ser mutation in P53 gene is associated with HCC and that the levels of sIL-2 R are significantly increased in liver cirrhoses and HCC patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
aflatoxin B 1 is an environmental factor that may contribute to hepatocarcinogenesis.
aflatoxin exposure and P53 mutations are important in the pathogenesis of HCC in our region.
aflatoxin B 1 exposure, HBV and HCV infections, and P53 & s IL-2R are involved in the pathogenesis of liver cirrhoses and hepatocellular carcinomas.
